questions.stem: What is the most important purpose of a balanced scorecard?
questions.explanation: The scorecard exists to measure performance, translating a strategy that already exists into a set of indicators across four perspectives so that progress can be tracked. Developing the strategy and setting priorities come first and are management's job; cause-and-effect linkages are a feature of the strategy map, not the purpose of the scorecard.
questions.explanationJa: バランスト・スコアカードは業績を測定するために存在する。既に策定された戦略を4つの視点にわたる指標群へ翻訳し、進捗を追跡できるようにするものである。戦略の策定と優先順位の設定はその前段階にある経営陣の仕事であり、因果関係の連鎖は戦略マップの特徴であって、スコアカードの目的ではない。

questions.stem: Which of the following is not one of the four perspectives of the balanced scorecard?
questions.explanation: The four perspectives are financial, customer, internal business processes, and learning and growth. Investment in resources is not one of them; spending on resources would appear as an input under the financial or learning and growth perspective rather than as a perspective of its own.
questions.explanationJa: 4つの視点とは、財務、顧客、内部業務プロセス、学習と成長である。資源への投資はその一つではない。資源への支出は、独立した視点としてではなく、財務または学習と成長の視点における投入要素として現れる。

questions.stem: The balanced scorecard generally uses performance measures with four different perspectives. Which of the following performance measures would be part of those used for the internal business processes perspective?
questions.explanation: The internal business processes perspective measures how well the work inside the organization is performed, and cycle time is the classic example. Employee satisfaction and training hours belong to learning and growth, and customer retention to the customer perspective.
questions.explanationJa: 内部業務プロセスの視点は、組織内部の業務がどれだけうまく遂行されているかを測るものであり、サイクルタイムがその代表例である。従業員満足度と研修時間は学習と成長の視点に、顧客維持率は顧客の視点に属する。

questions.stem:
The balanced scorecard has been adopted by many corporations. Which of the following best describes
the balanced scorecard?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A strategy that meets management’s objectives.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A diagram illustrating cause and effect relationships.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A table of key actions to achieve strategic objectives.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A strategic performance measurement and management framework.

questions.explanation: The scorecard is a framework: it takes a strategy and converts it into objectives, measures, targets, and initiatives across four perspectives, then uses those measures to manage execution. It is not itself a strategy, nor is it the strategy map (choice B) or the initiatives list (choice C), both of which are parts of the framework.
questions.explanationJa: スコアカードは枠組みである。戦略を受け取り、4つの視点にわたる目標・測定指標・目標値・施策へ変換したうえで、それらの指標を用いて実行を管理する。それ自体が戦略なのではなく、戦略マップ（選択肢B）でも施策一覧（選択肢C）でもない。後の2つはこの枠組みの構成要素である。

questions.stem: The balanced scorecard and value-based management are techniques that are being used by a number of corporations. In comparison to the balanced scorecard, value-based management focuses on
questions.explanation: Value-based management keeps a single financial yardstick, shareholder value, and drives every decision toward increasing it, typically through measures such as economic value added. The balanced scorecard deliberately sets financial measures alongside nonfinancial ones.
questions.explanationJa: 価値基準経営（value-based management）は、株主価値という単一の財務尺度を保ち、あらゆる意思決定をその増大へ向ける手法であり、通常は経済的付加価値（EVA）のような指標を用いる。バランスト・スコアカードは、財務指標に非財務指標を意図的に並置する点で異なる。

questions.stem: Management has identified a relationship between customer satisfaction and return on investment. This relationship could be depicted in a
questions.explanation: A strategy map is the diagram that shows how objectives in one perspective drive objectives in another, for example how higher customer satisfaction feeds through to higher return on investment. The value chain describes the sequence of processes, and the initiatives list records the action programs.
questions.explanationJa: 戦略マップは、ある視点の目標が別の視点の目標をどう押し上げるかを示す図であり、たとえば顧客満足度の向上が投資収益率の向上へつながる経路を表す。バリューチェーンは業務の連鎖を記述するものであり、施策一覧は実行プログラムを記録するものである。

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a component of the balanced scorecard?
questions.explanation: The components are strategic objectives, performance measures, targets for those measures, and the strategic initiatives that will achieve them. Assessing human resources is an activity that may support the learning and growth perspective, not a structural component of the scorecard.
questions.explanationJa: スコアカードの構成要素は、戦略目標、業績測定指標、それらの指標に対する目標値、そしてそれを達成するための戦略的施策である。人的資源の評価は学習と成長の視点を支える活動でありうるが、スコアカードの構造上の構成要素ではない。

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes a value chain in the balanced scorecard framework?

choices.label: C
choices.text: The sequence of business processes in which usefulness is added to products or services.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The chain of financial and nonfinancial measures.

questions.explanation: The value chain is the ordered set of processes, from innovation through operations to after-sales service, each of which adds usefulness to the product or service. In the scorecard it underlies the internal business processes perspective. Cause-and-effect linkages belong to the strategy map.
questions.explanationJa: バリューチェーンとは、革新から業務、そしてアフターサービスに至るまで、順序づけられた一連の業務の集合であり、その各段階が製品やサービスに有用性を付加していく。スコアカードにおいては内部業務プロセスの視点の基礎となる。因果関係の連鎖は戦略マップに属する概念である。

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a characteristic of the balanced scorecard?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Both financial and nonfinancial performance measures are included.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Internal process performance measures are included.

questions.explanation: Customer measures are one of the four perspectives, so excluding them contradicts the whole design. The other three statements are accurate: the scorecard mixes financial and nonfinancial measures, links objectives causally, and includes internal process measures.
questions.explanationJa: 顧客に関する指標は4つの視点の一つなので、これを除外するという記述は設計思想そのものと矛盾する。他の3つの記述は正確である。スコアカードは財務指標と非財務指標を組み合わせ、目標同士を因果関係で結び、内部プロセスの指標を含む。

questions.stem: In the balanced scorecard framework, employee retention is a potential measure in which of the four perspectives?
questions.explanation: Learning and growth covers the organization's people, systems, and culture, the infrastructure that makes future improvement possible. Employee retention measures whether that human capital is being preserved, so it belongs there rather than to any of the outcome-oriented perspectives.
questions.explanationJa: 学習と成長の視点は、組織の人材・システム・文化、すなわち将来の改善を可能にする基盤を扱う。従業員の定着率はその人的資本が維持されているかを測る指標なので、成果を扱う他の視点ではなくここに属する。

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of an efficiency measure?

choices.label: B
choices.text: The goal of becoming a leading manufacturer.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The number of insurance claims processed per day.

questions.explanation: Efficiency compares output to input, so it takes the form of a ratio such as claims processed per day, that is, units of work per unit of resource. Absenteeism and complaint rates are quality or effectiveness indicators, and becoming a leading manufacturer is a goal, not a measure.
questions.explanationJa: 効率性は産出を投入と比較するものなので、1日当たりの処理件数のような比率、すなわち資源1単位当たりの仕事量という形をとる。欠勤率と苦情発生率は品質または有効性の指標であり、主要メーカーになることは目標であって測定指標ではない。

questions.stem: A strategy objective in the balanced scorecard framework is

choices.label: A
choices.text: A statement of what the strategy must achieve and what is critical to its success.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Key action programs required to achieve strategic objectives.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Diagrams of the cause-and-effect relationships between strategic objectives.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The level of performance or rate of improvement needed in the performance measure.

questions.explanation: A strategic objective states what the strategy has to accomplish and what is critical to its success, for example to shorten delivery time. The other three define the initiative (B), the strategy map (C), and the target (D).
questions.explanationJa: 戦略目標は、戦略が何を達成しなければならないか、そして成功のために何が決定的かを述べるものであり、たとえば「納期を短縮する」といった形をとる。他の3つはそれぞれ施策（B）、戦略マップ（C）、目標値（D）の定義である。

questions.stem: A target in the balanced scorecard framework is

choices.label: A
choices.text: A statement of what the strategy must achieve and what is critical to its success.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A key action program required to achieve strategic objectives.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A diagram of the cause-and-effect relationships between strategic objectives.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The level of performance or rate of improvement needed in the performance measure.

questions.explanation: A target puts a number on a measure: the level to reach or the rate of improvement required, such as cutting delivery time to two days. The objective says what matters, the measure says how it is tracked, and the initiative says what will be done.
questions.explanationJa: 目標値（target）は測定指標に数値を与えるものであり、到達すべき水準や要求される改善率を示す。たとえば「納期を2日に短縮する」といった形である。戦略目標は何が重要かを述べ、測定指標はそれをどう追跡するかを示し、施策は何を実行するかを定める。

questions.explanation: The DuPont identity: ROI = (net income / sales) x (sales / invested capital), that is, profit margin multiplied by the capital turnover rate. The sales term cancels, leaving net income over invested capital.

questions.stem:
The following information pertains to Bala Co. for the year ended December 31, 2014:
Sales | $600,000
Net income | 100,000
Capital investment | 400,000
Which of the following equations should be used to compute Bala’s return on investment?
questions.explanation: ROI = profit margin x capital turnover = ($100 / $600) x ($600 / $400), which in the answer's shorthand is (1/6) x (6/4). Choice B states the same two factors in the opposite order, and multiplication is commutative, so it gives the same 25%.
questions.explanationJa: ROI = 売上高利益率 × 資本回転率 = ($100 ÷ $600) × ($600 ÷ $400) であり、選択肢の略記では (1/6) × (6/4) にあたる。選択肢Bは同じ2つの要素を逆の順で並べたものだが、掛け算は順序を入れ替えても同じなので、結果は同じ25%となる。

What was Select’s 2014 percentage return on assets?
questions.explanation: Return on assets = profit margin x asset turnover = 0.02 x 5 = 0.10, or 10%. Dividing instead of multiplying gives 0.4%, which is choice B.
questions.explanationJa: 総資産利益率 = 売上高利益率 × 資産回転率 = 0.02 × 5 = 0.10、すなわち10%。掛けるべきところを割ると0.4%となり、選択肢Bに落ちる。

questions.stem:
The following selected data pertain to the Darwin Division of Beagle Co. for 2014:
Sales | $400,000
Net income | 40,000
Capital turnover | 4
Imputed interest rate | 10%
What was Darwin’s 2014 residual income?
questions.explanation: Capital turnover is sales divided by invested capital, so invested capital = $400,000 / 4 = $100,000. Residual income = $40,000 - ($100,000 x 10%) = $30,000. Applying the 10% to sales instead of to capital would give $0, which is choice A.
questions.explanationJa: 資本回転率は売上高を投下資本で割ったものなので、投下資本 = $400,000 ÷ 4 = $100,000。残余利益 = $40,000 − ($100,000 × 10%) = $30,000。10%を資本ではなく売上高に適用すると $0 となり、選択肢Aに落ちる。

questions.stem:
Division A is considering a project that will earn a rate of return which is greater than the imputed interest charge for invested capital, but less than the division’s historical return on invested capital. Division B is considering a project that will earn a rate of return that is greater than the division’s historical return on invested capital, but less than the imputed interest charge for invested capital. If the objective is to maximize residual income, should these divisions accept or reject their projects?
A | B
questions.explanation: Residual income rises whenever a project earns more than the imputed interest charge, whatever the division's historical average happens to be. Division A clears that hurdle and should accept; Division B does not and should reject, even though the project would beat its own past return. Judging by the historical return instead is exactly the distortion that residual income is designed to remove.
questions.explanationJa: 残余利益は、そのプロジェクトが資本費用の賦課率を上回って稼ぐ限り増加する。事業部の過去の平均収益率がいくらであるかは関係しない。A事業部はこのハードルを越えているので採択すべきであり、B事業部は越えていないので、自部門の過去の収益率は上回るとしても却下すべきである。過去の収益率で判断してしまうことこそ、残余利益が取り除こうとする歪みそのものである。

choices.label: A
choices.text: Residual income is a measure over time while ROI represents the results for a single time period.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Residual income concentrates on maximizing absolute dollars of income rather than a percentage return as with ROI.

choices.label: C

choices.label: D

questions.explanation: A manager judged on ROI will reject any project earning less than the division's current ROI, even when it exceeds the cost of capital, because accepting it would drag the percentage down. Residual income measures dollars of income above the capital charge, so every project that clears the cost of capital increases it, which aligns the division's incentive with the firm's.
questions.explanationJa: ROIで評価される管理者は、資本コストを上回るプロジェクトであっても、自部門の現在のROIを下回るものは却下してしまう。受け入れれば比率が下がるからである。残余利益は資本費用を上回る利益を金額で測るので、資本コストを超えるプロジェクトはすべて残余利益を増やすことになり、事業部の誘因が企業全体の利益と一致する。

questions.stem: What is a major disadvantage of using economic value added (EVA) alone as a performance measure?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It fails to focus on creating shareholder value.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It promotes the acceptance of unprofitable projects.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It fails to reflect all of the ways that value may be created.

questions.explanation: EVA is a single financial number covering one period, so it captures none of the drivers that build value over time: customer loyalty, process quality, employee capability, and innovation. Used alone it can be improved by cutting the very spending that creates those assets, which is why it is normally paired with nonfinancial measures.
questions.explanationJa: EVAは1期間を対象とする単一の財務数値なので、時間をかけて価値を築く要因、すなわち顧客の忠誠度、業務の品質、従業員の能力、革新のいずれも捉えられない。単独で用いると、まさにそれらを生み出す支出を削ることで数値を改善できてしまう。非財務指標と組み合わせて使うのが通例なのはそのためである。

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a measure of asset utilization?
questions.explanation: Asset utilization ratios pair a flow with the assets that produced it, showing how hard the assets work: inventory turnover, receivable collection period, and fixed asset turnover all do this. Debt to total assets compares financing to assets, which makes it a leverage ratio.
questions.explanationJa: 資産効率の指標は、フローとそれを生み出した資産を対応させ、資産がどれだけ働いているかを示す。棚卸資産回転率、売掛金回収期間、固定資産回転率はいずれもこれにあたる。負債比率（負債 ÷ 総資産）は資金調達と資産を比較するものであり、レバレッジの指標である。

questions.stem: What financial analysis technique would imply benchmarking with other firms?
questions.explanation: Cross-sectional analysis compares the company with other firms at the same point in time, which is what benchmarking means. Horizontal analysis compares the company with its own prior periods, vertical analysis expresses items as a percentage of a base within one statement, and ratio analysis is the underlying tool used in all of them.
questions.explanationJa: クロスセクション分析は、同一時点における他社との比較であり、これがベンチマーキングの意味するところである。趨勢分析（horizontal analysis）は自社の過去の期間との比較、百分率分析（vertical analysis）は一つの財務諸表内で各項目を基準値に対する割合で表すもの、比率分析はそのいずれにも用いられる基礎的な手法である。

questions.explanation: Work down the income statement. EBIT $35M - interest $5M = $30M pre-tax; after 40% tax, net income is $18M; preferred dividends of $4M leave $14M for common. The 30% payout is $4.2M, and over 2 million shares that is $2.10 per share. Forgetting the preferred dividends gives $2.70, which is choice B.
questions.explanationJa: 損益計算書を上から順にたどる。EBIT $35M − 支払利息 $5M = 税引前利益 $30M。40%課税後の当期純利益は $18M。優先株配当 $4M を差し引くと普通株主に帰属するのは $14M。配当性向30%で $4.2M、これを200万株で割ると1株当たり $2.10。優先株配当を忘れると $2.70 となり、選択肢Bに落ちる。

choices.text: Affects all of the answers as indicated.

questions.explanation: The building is not a current asset, but the installment due within the year is a current liability. Current liabilities therefore rise with no change in current assets: working capital falls, and both the current and the quick ratio fall.
questions.explanationJa: 建物は流動資産ではないが、1年以内に期限の到来する分割払いの部分は流動負債となる。したがって流動資産が変わらないまま流動負債だけが増える。正味運転資本は減少し、流動比率も当座比率もともに低下する。

Depoole Company is a manufacturer of industrial products and employs a calendar year for financial reporting purposes. Assume that Depoole's total quick assets exceeded total current liabilities both before and after the transaction. Further assume that Depoole has positive profits during the year and a credit balance throughout the year in its retained earnings account.

Assume that Depoole's total quick assets exceeded total current liabilities both before and after the transaction. Further assume that Depoole has positive profits during the year and a credit balance throughout the year in its retained earnings account.
Depoole Company is a manufacturer of industrial products and employs a calendar year for financial reporting purposes. Assume that Depoole's total quick assets exceeded total current liabilities both before and after the transaction. Further assume that Depoole has positive profits during the year and a credit balance throughout the year in its retained earnings account.
The early liquidation of a long-term note with cash affects the

choices.label: A
choices.text: Current ratio to a greater degree than the quick ratio.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Quick ratio to a greater degree than the current ratio.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Current and quick ratio to the same degree.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Current ratio but not the quick ratio.

questions.explanation: Paying off a long-term note uses cash, a quick asset, while current liabilities are unchanged, so both ratios fall by the same number of points. Since the quick ratio starts from a smaller base, that identical drop is proportionally larger, so it is affected to the greater degree. Note that choice B contains a typo in the source material, comparing the quick ratio with itself; the intended comparison is with the current ratio.
questions.explanationJa: 長期の約束手形の返済は当座資産である現金を減らす一方、流動負債は変わらないので、両方の比率が同じ幅だけ低下する。当座比率はもともと分子が小さいので、同じ幅の低下でも割合としては大きく、より大きな影響を受けることになる。なお選択肢Bは教材側の誤植で当座比率を当座比率と比較する文になっており、本来は流動比率との比較である。

questions.stem: Southwest Airlines benchmarked the process of turning around an airplane with the pit stop process for formula racecars. This is an example of
questions.explanation: Comparing an aircraft turnaround with a racing pit stop takes a process from a completely unrelated industry, which is generic benchmarking. Functional benchmarking looks at the same business function in other industries, competitor benchmarking at direct rivals, and internal benchmarking at other units of the same company.
questions.explanationJa: 航空機の折り返し作業をレースのピット作業と比較することは、まったく無関係な業界からプロセスを借りてくることであり、これがジェネリック・ベンチマーキングである。機能別ベンチマーキングは他業界における同じ業務機能を対象とし、競合ベンチマーキングは直接の競争相手を、内部ベンチマーキングは自社の他部門を対象とする。

questions.stem:
Which measures would be useful in evaluating the performance of a manufacturing system?
I. Throughput time.
II. Total setup time for machines/Total production time.
III. Number of rework units/Total number of units completed.
questions.explanation: All three are operational measures of a manufacturing system. Throughput time measures speed, the setup-to-production ratio measures how much capacity is lost to changeovers, and the rework ratio measures quality. Together they cover time, efficiency, and defects.
questions.explanationJa: 3つとも製造システムの業務指標である。スループット・タイムは速さを、段取時間対生産時間の比率は段取替えによって失われる能力の割合を、手直し比率は品質を測る。3つ合わせて、時間・効率・不良の各側面を網羅する。

questions.stem: A tool which indicates how frequently each type of defect occurs is a
questions.explanation: A Pareto diagram ranks defect types by frequency in a descending bar chart, making visible the few categories that account for most of the problems. A control chart tracks a process over time, and the cause-and-effect (fishbone) diagram traces why a defect occurs rather than how often.
questions.explanationJa: パレート図は不良の類型を発生頻度の降順で棒グラフに並べ、問題の大半を占める少数のカテゴリーを可視化する。管理図はプロセスを時系列で追跡するものであり、特性要因図（フィッシュボーン図）は不良が起きる頻度ではなく原因をたどるものである。

questions.stem: A tool which identifies potential causes for failures or defects is
questions.explanation: The cause-and-effect diagram, also called a fishbone or Ishikawa diagram, arranges potential causes along branches by category, typically materials, methods, machines, and people, so that a team can work back from a defect to its sources. Note that choice D in this question is the same tool under its other name.
questions.explanationJa: 特性要因図は、フィッシュボーン図あるいは石川ダイアグラムとも呼ばれ、潜在的な原因を材料・方法・機械・人といったカテゴリー別の枝に整理し、不良から原因へさかのぼって検討できるようにする。なおこの設問の選択肢Dは、同じ手法の別名にすぎない点に注意したい。

questions.stem: Which of the statement best describes the concept of six-sigma quality?
questions.explanation: Six sigma sets the process spread so that virtually nothing falls outside specification: allowing for the customary 1.5 sigma long-run drift in the process mean, the target works out to 3.4 defects per million opportunities.
questions.explanationJa: シックス・シグマは、規格外がほぼ発生しないところまでプロセスのばらつきを抑える考え方である。慣行として工程平均の長期的な1.5シグマのずれを見込むと、目標は100万機会あたり3.4件の不良となる。

questions.stem: Which of the following quality tools is another term for continuous improvement?
questions.explanation: Kaizen is the practice of many small, incremental improvements made continuously by the people doing the work. Six sigma is a defect-reduction methodology, lean manufacturing targets waste, and the theory of constraints focuses on the bottleneck.
questions.explanationJa: カイゼンは、現場で働く人々が継続的に小さな改善を数多く積み重ねていく取り組みである。シックス・シグマは不良削減の方法論、リーン生産方式はムダの排除、制約理論はボトルネックへの集中を狙うものである。

questions.stem: In considering cost of quality methodology, quality circles are associated with
questions.explanation: Quality circles are groups of employees who meet to find and remove the causes of defects before they occur, so their cost is a prevention cost. Appraisal is inspection of what has already been made, and the two failure categories arise only after a defect exists.
questions.explanationJa: QCサークルは、不良が発生する前にその原因を見つけて取り除くために従業員が集まる活動なので、そのコストは予防コストにあたる。評価コストは既に作られたものを検査する費用であり、2つの失敗コストは不良が生じて初めて発生する。

questions.stem: In the cost of qualify, which of the following is an example of an “internal failure”?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cost of inspecting products on the production line by quality inspectors.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Labor cost of product designers whose task is to design components that will not break under extreme temperature conditions.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cost of reworking defective parts detected by the quality assurance group.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cost of parts returned by customers.

questions.explanation: Internal failure costs arise when a defect is found before the product reaches the customer, and reworking parts caught by quality assurance is the textbook case. Inspection is appraisal, design work is prevention, and returns from customers are external failure.
questions.explanationJa: 内部失敗コストは、製品が顧客に届く前に不良が発見された場合に生じるものであり、品質保証部門が検出した部品の手直しはその典型例である。検査は評価コスト、設計作業は予防コスト、顧客からの返品は外部失敗コストにあたる。

questions.stem: In the cost of quality, which of the following is an example of a “prevention cost”?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cost of inspecting products on the production line by quality inspectors.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Labor cost of product designers whose task is to design components that will not break under extreme temperature conditions.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cost of reworking defective parts detected by the quality assurance group.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cost of parts returned by customers.

questions.explanation: Prevention costs are incurred before production to stop defects from arising at all. Designing components that will withstand extreme temperatures builds quality into the product itself, which is prevention in its purest form.
questions.explanationJa: 予防コストは、そもそも不良が生じないようにするために生産前に投じる費用である。極端な温度条件でも壊れない部品を設計することは、製品そのものに品質を作り込む行為であり、最も純粋な意味での予防にあたる。

questions.stem: Delta Manufacturing Co. has had a problem with its product quality. The company has had a large amount of costs related to product recalls. In considering cost of quality methodology, if the company wants to reduce these costs, the most likely place to incur costs would be for
questions.explanation: Recalls are external failure costs, the most expensive category because they include the customer's loss and the damage to reputation. Spending more on prevention attacks the defects at their source, and the total cost of quality normally falls even though prevention spending rises.
questions.explanationJa: リコールは外部失敗コストであり、顧客側の損失や評判の毀損まで含むため最も高くつく分類である。予防に支出を増やすことは不良を源で断つことであり、予防コストが増えても品質コストの総額は通常むしろ減少する。

questions.stem: In the cost of quality, cost incurred in detecting individual units of product that do not conform to specifications are
questions.explanation: Appraisal costs are the costs of finding out whether individual units meet specification: inspection, testing, and measurement. They neither prevent the defect nor repair it, they only detect it.
questions.explanationJa: 評価コストとは、個々の製品が規格を満たしているかどうかを確かめるための費用であり、検査・試験・測定がこれにあたる。不良を防ぐわけでも直すわけでもなく、検出するだけの費用である。

questions.stem: In an attempt to improve operations, companies often go through analyses and redesign of the way processes are performed. Which of the following is not considered to be an aspect of a business process that may be focused on to achieve improvement?

choices.label: C
choices.text: The interaction between technology and human performance.

questions.explanation: Process improvement works on how the work is actually done: the technology used, the people performing it, and the interaction between them. Strategic goals are the ends the processes serve and are set outside the redesign; changing them is not process improvement.
questions.explanationJa: プロセス改善が対象とするのは、仕事が実際にどう行われているかであり、使用する技術、それを遂行する人、そして両者の相互作用である。戦略目標はプロセスが奉仕する目的であって、再設計の外側で設定されるものであり、これを変えることはプロセス改善ではない。

questions.stem: Management of organizations that engage in business process management view business processes as

choices.label: A
choices.text: Requirements for good control over the organization.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Systems that provide information for good management.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Strategic assets that must be understood, managed and improved.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mechanisms that keep employees from shirking.

questions.explanation: Business process management treats processes as strategic assets in their own right, on the view that how a company executes is itself a source of competitive advantage, so processes must be documented, owned, measured, and continuously improved rather than merely controlled.
questions.explanationJa: ビジネスプロセス・マネジメントは、プロセスそれ自体を戦略資産とみなす。企業が「どう実行するか」自体が競争優位の源泉であるという見方に立つので、プロセスは単に統制するのではなく、文書化し、責任者を定め、測定し、継続的に改善しなければならない。

questions.stem: At which phase in the business process management lifecycle does management simulate performance of the process in a test environment?
questions.explanation: The lifecycle runs design, modeling, execution, monitoring, and optimization. Modeling is where the design is run with different variables in a test environment to see how it would behave before any live commitment is made.
questions.explanationJa: このライフサイクルは、設計・モデリング・実行・監視・最適化の順に進む。モデリングは、実運用に踏み切る前にテスト環境で変数を変えながら設計を動かし、どのように振る舞うかを確かめる段階である。

questions.stem: In the theory of constraints, an operation or resource where the work performed approaches or exceeds the available time is referred to as
questions.explanation: A bottleneck is the resource whose capacity is at or below the demand placed on it, so it sets the pace of the whole system. Under the theory of constraints, output can only be increased by relieving that constraint; effort spent elsewhere just builds inventory in front of it.
questions.explanationJa: ボトルネックとは、要求される作業量に対して能力が同等かそれ以下の資源であり、システム全体のペースを決めてしまう。制約理論では、産出を増やせるのはその制約を緩和したときだけであり、他の場所に労力を注いでもボトルネックの手前に仕掛品が積み上がるだけである。

questions.stem:
Which statement best describes the objective of the theory of constraints?
Throughput contribution | Investment | Operating costs
questions.explanation: The theory of constraints aims to increase throughput contribution, sales less direct materials, while reducing both investment, mainly inventory, and operating costs. Throughput is the priority because it has no ceiling, whereas the two cost reductions can only go so far.
questions.explanationJa: 制約理論の狙いは、スループット貢献（売上高から直接材料費を差し引いたもの）を増やしつつ、投資（主として在庫）と業務費用の両方を減らすことにある。スループットが優先されるのは、それには上限がないのに対し、2つのコスト削減には限界があるからである。

questions.stem: Which of the following involves comparing measures of actual progress of a project to planned progress?
questions.explanation: Project control is the ongoing comparison of actual progress, cost, and quality against the plan, together with the corrective action that follows. Planning sets the scope and approach, scheduling fixes the sequence and dates, and closure wraps the project up.
questions.explanationJa: プロジェクト・コントロールとは、進捗・コスト・品質の実績を計画と継続的に比較し、それに続く是正措置を講じることである。計画立案は範囲と進め方を定め、スケジューリングは順序と日程を確定し、終結は案件を締めくくる段階である。

questions.stem: Which of the following is a detailed listing of the man-hour, equipment, and materials requirements for a project?
questions.explanation: Project specifications set out in detail what the project needs in man-hours, equipment, and materials. The statement of work describes the objectives and deliverables in narrative form, the work breakdown structure decomposes the project into tasks, and the milestone schedule lists key dates.
questions.explanationJa: プロジェクト仕様書（project specifications）は、そのプロジェクトに必要な工数・設備・材料を詳細に定めたものである。作業指示書（statement of work）は目的と成果物を文章で記述し、WBSはプロジェクトを作業単位へ分解し、マイルストーン・スケジュールは重要な期日を列挙するものである。

questions.stem: Which of the following is used to describe the practice of adding resources to shorten selected activity time on the critical path of a project?
questions.explanation: Crashing means buying time with money: extra resources are put on critical path activities to shorten them, accepting higher cost for an earlier finish. Only critical path activities are worth crashing, since shortening an activity with slack does not move the completion date.
questions.explanationJa: クラッシングとは、資金で時間を買うことである。クリティカルパス上の作業に資源を追加投入して所要時間を短縮し、完了を早める代わりにコストの増加を受け入れる。クラッシングする価値があるのはクリティカルパス上の作業だけである。余裕（スラック）のある作業を短縮しても完了日は動かないからである。

questions.stem:
When a project can be completed in a number of completely different ways that might involve branching
after performing activities, the best schedule and control technique would be
questions.explanation: GERT allows branching and looping, so a network can contain alternative routes and activities that may be repeated or skipped depending on outcomes. CPM and PERT both assume every activity is performed once in a fixed sequence, and a Gantt chart is a bar schedule with no network logic at all.
questions.explanationJa: GERTは分岐とループを扱えるので、結果に応じて代替経路をとったり、作業を繰り返したり省略したりするネットワークを表現できる。CPMもPERTも、すべての作業が固定された順序で1回ずつ実行されることを前提とし、ガントチャートに至ってはネットワーク論理を持たない棒状の日程表にすぎない。

questions.stem: A technique that is often used in project management to identify tasks where attention should be focused because they are the most critical or valuable is referred to as
questions.explanation: ABC analysis sorts items into a small group of high-value or high-criticality items and progressively larger groups of less important ones, so that management attention goes where it matters most. It is the same Pareto logic used in inventory control, applied to project tasks.
questions.explanationJa: ABC分析は、対象を「価値または重要度の高い少数の項目」から「重要度の低い多数の項目」へと段階的に分類し、経営の注意を最も重要なところへ向けさせる手法である。在庫管理で使われるのと同じパレートの論理を、プロジェクトの作業に適用したものである。
